description: Fisher's exact test on the 2x2 table [[a, b], [c, d]]: the sample odds ratio a d / (b c) and the p-value from the hypergeometric distribution of the first cell with all margins fixed; alternative -1 less (P(X <= a)), 0 two-sided (the sum of P(x) over every x with P(x) <= P(a), compared exactly, at most 1), 1 greater (P(X >= a))

tolerance.reason: For both outputs, by the rule of ttest_1samp. The inputs are whole numbers (condition number 0) and the p-value is a ratio of exact counts (kappa_p = 1), so only rounding counts: n 2^-53 with n the number of hypergeometric terms in the support, a generous count for a careful sum of the smaller tail (fisher_exact_rounding_bound). The largest bound on this grid is 7.8e-14 (margins 1000, 900, 700: 701 terms); 1e-13 is the smallest round value above it (tested). The odds ratio is two products and a quotient, exact or within 2 ulp

grid: Published tables (SciPy's documentation, Fisher's tea tasting, statrs's fisher test cases: 10 tables), the first 12 tables (by total, then n1 <= n <= n2) whose probability is below another table's by at most 1e-4 relative (the first is (6, 9, 16, 41)), and tables by their margins (n1 = a + b, n2 = c + d, n = a + c) in {(3, 5, 4), (5, 5, 5), (10, 10, 8), (8, 30, 12), (20, 20, 20), (50, 40, 30), (100, 100, 100), (200, 50, 60), (400, 400, 400), (600, 600, 300), (1000, 900, 700)} with a at both ends of its support, next to them, at the mode, and at the mean + k sd for k in {+-8, +-4, +-2, +-1, +-0.5, 0}; each with alternative -1 (less), 0 (two-sided) and 1 (greater). No row or column sum is zero, and b c > 0 (an infinite odds ratio would be tagged overflow, and a finite p-value at an overflow point is judged crate wrong), which leaves out a at the top of its support
